label: 1.1.1-opus-high
messages: /tokenwise:route implement a feature from a written spec, about 12 files
/tokenwise:route review a six-file diff in a repo I know well

result:
- **Phase:** Implement a feature from a written spec, about 12 files.
- **Model and effort:** `/model sonnet` then `/effort medium`.
- **Boundary:** Make sure the spec is saved to a file, then `/clear`, then switch model and effort, then start from the spec file. If you switch on a warm context instead, your whole current context gets re-processed on the new model. `/context` shows how big that is. This answer also stays in your context until your next `/clear`, so running `/clear` straight after reading it costs least.
- **Delegate:**
  - Before starting the session, set `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL=haiku` and `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE=1` (needs Claude Code 2.1.257 or later). Without the second variable, Explore uses your session model.
  - Send codebase exploration for the 12 files, test runs and log reading to subagents so only their summaries come back.
  - The spec itself stays in the main context.
- **Done when:** the project's test command passes and `git diff --stat` shows no test files edited. Run lint and typecheck too if the project has them. Do this before starting a review phase.
- **You give up:** Sonnet makes the calls on anything the spec leaves out, and it is less reliable there than Opus. The bench evidence (Sonnet at medium passed every run at 17% of the cost of Opus at xhigh) comes from a small test project. A 12-file change is bigger than that, so the result may not hold at this size.
- **Escalate when:**
  - **It didn't try hard enough** (skipped files, didn't run the tests, stopped partway): stay on Sonnet and raise effort to `/effort high`, then `xhigh`. On the bench, Sonnet at xhigh cost less per completed task than Opus at medium.
  - **It got things wrong with the context it had** (misread the spec, wrong design, fixes that keep failing): switch to `/model opus` at `medium`, then `xhigh`. Make the switch after a `/clear`, starting again from the spec file.

- Phase: review a six-file diff in a repo you know well
- Model and effort: `/model opus` then `/effort low`
- Boundary: the model is the only thing that matters here. If you're already on opus, change effort in place, since effort doesn't touch the cache. If you're on another model, `/clear` first so the switch costs nothing. Switching on a warm context re-processes all of it, and `/context` shows how big that is. This answer stays in your context until your next `/clear`, so routing just before one costs least.
- Delegate: nothing. Six files is small enough to read in the main context, and a subagent would only add overhead here.
- Done when: every finding gives a file:line and a concrete input that fails. A finding without both isn't done.
- You give up: low effort makes fewer tool calls and does less cross-checking. It won't go hunting through callers outside the diff or run tests unless you ask. On a six-file bench diff, low found the same five planted defects as high in 3 turns against 13, at a third of the cost. That's one small test project, so it's evidence, not a guarantee for your repo.
- Escalate when: two different signals.
  - If the review skipped files in the diff or never checked a changed caller, it didn't try hard enough. Raise effort to `/effort high` and stay on opus.
  - If it read everything and still missed or misread a defect you can point to, stay on opus at high. On the bench, sonnet at high missed a defect in two of three runs, so it isn't a cheaper fallback.
  - If the diff turns out bigger or less familiar than you expected, start at opus `high`.
